'''Rudolf Haag''' (17 August 1922 – 5 January 2016) was a German theoretical [[physicist]], who mainly dealt with fundamental questions of [[quantum field theory]]. He was one of the founders of the modern formulation of quantum field theory, and he identified the formal structure in terms of the [[principle of locality]] and local [[observable]]s. He also made important advances in the foundations of [[quantum statistical mechanics]].<ref name=HP_citation>{{cite web |url=http://www.iamp.org/poincare/rh97-cit.html|title=Henri Poincaré Prize citation|website=International Association of Mathematical Physics|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Rudolf Haag was born on 17 August 1922, in [[Tübingen]], a university town in the middle of [[Baden-Württemberg]]. His family belonged to the cultured middle class. Haag's mother was the writer and politician Anna Haag.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Haag|first1=Rudolf|last2=Haag|first2=Anna|date=2003|edition=1|title=Leben und gelebt werden: Erinnerungen und Betrachtungen|publisher=Silberburg|language=de|isbn=978-3874075626}} {{Cite book|last=Timms|first=Edward|date=2016|title=Anna Haag and her Secret Diary of the Second World War: A Democratic German Feminist's Response to the Catastrophe of National Socialism|publisher=Peter Lang AG, Internationaler Verlag der Wissenschaften|isbn=978-3034318181}}</ref> His father, Albert Haag, was a teacher of [[mathematics]] at a [[Gymnasium (school)|Gymnasium]]. After finishing [[high-school]] in 1939, he visited his sister in [[London]] shortly before the beginning of [[World War II]]. He was [[interned]] as an [[enemy alien]] and spent the war in a camp of German civilians in [[Manitoba]]. There he used his spare-time after the daily compulsory labour to study [[physics]] and mathematics as an [[autodidact]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last = Kastler|first = Daniel|title = Rudolf Haag – Eighty years|journal = Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume = 237|pages = 3–6|year = 2003|issue = 1–2|doi = 10.1007/s00220-003-0829-1|bibcode = 2003CMaPh.237....3K|s2cid = 121438414}}</ref>

After the war, Haag returned to Germany and enrolled at the [[Technische Hochschule Stuttgart]] in 1946, where he graduated as a physicist in 1948. In 1951, he received his [[doctorate]] at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]] under the supervision of [[Fritz Bopp]]<ref>The doctoral thesis is {{cite thesis|last=Haag|first=Rudolf|date=1951|title=Die korrespondenzmässige Methode in der Theorie der Elementarteilchen|lang=de|url=https://opac.ub.uni-muenchen.de/TouchPoint/perma.do?q=+0%3D%225363125%22+IN+%5B2%5D&l=en|place=Munich}}</ref> and became his assistant until 1956. In April 1953, he joined the [[CERN]] theoretical study group in [[Copenhagen]]{{refn|group=note|Since the laboratory in [[Geneva]] was still under construction, the study group was hosted by the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] in Copenhagen.<ref>{{Cite book|last = Poggendorff|first = Johann C.|date = 1958|title = J.C. Poggendorffs biographisch-literarisches Handwörterbuch zur Geschichte der exacten Wissenschaften|publisher = J.A. Barth|language=de}}</ref>}} directed by [[Niels Bohr]].<ref name=Haag2010>{{Cite journal|last = Haag|first = Rudolf|title = Some people and some problems met in half a century of commitment to mathematical physics|journal = The European Physical Journal H|volume = 35|pages = 263–307|year = 2010|issue = 3|doi = 10.1140/epjh/e2010-10032-4|bibcode = 2010EPJH...35..263H|s2cid = 59320730}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timeline.web.cern.ch/closure-cerns-theoretical-study-division-copenhagen|title=Closure of CERN's Theoretical Study Division in Copenhagen
|website=timeline.web.cern.ch|access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref> After a year, he returned to his assistant position in Munich and completed the German [[habilitation]] in 1954.<ref>The habilitation thesis is {{cite thesis|last=Haag|first=Rudolf|date=1954|publication-date=1955|title=On Quantum field theories|lang=en|volume=29|number=12|publisher=Munksgaard in Komm.|url=https://opac.ub.uni-muenchen.de/TouchPoint/perma.do?q=+0%3D%225874215%22+IN+%5B2%5D&l=en|place=Copenaghen}}</ref> From 1956 to 1957, he worked with [[Werner Heisenberg]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Physics]] in [[Göttingen]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Buchholz|first1=Detlev|last2=Fredenhagen|first2=Klaus|title=Nachruf auf Rudolf Haag|journal=Physik Journal|volume=15|number=4|pages=53|year=2016|language=de|url=https://www.pro-physik.de/restricted-files/85781}}</ref>

From 1957 to 1959, he was a visiting professor at [[Princeton University]] and from 1959 to 1960 he worked at [[Aix-Marseille University]]. He became a professor of Physics at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] in 1960. In 1965, he and [[Res Jost]] founded the journal ''[[Communications in Mathematical Physics]]''. Haag remained the first editor-in-chief until 1973.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Jaffe|first1 = Arthur|last2 = Rehren|first2 = Karl-Henning|title = Rudolf Haag|journal = Physics Today|pages = 70–71|year = 2016|volume = 69|issue = 7|doi = 10.1063/PT.3.3244|bibcode = 2016PhT....69g..70J|doi-access = free}}</ref> In 1966, he accepted the professorship position for theoretical physics at the [[University of Hamburg]], where he stayed until he retired in 1987.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1 = Schönhammer|first1 = Kurt|title = Nachruf auf Rudolf Haag. 17. August 1922 – 5. Januar 2016|journal = Jahrbuch der Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen|pages = 236–237|year = 2016|language = de|doi = 10.1515/jbg-2016-0026|s2cid = 188592087}}</ref> After retirement, he worked on the concept of the quantum physical [[event (particle physics)|event]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last = Haag|first = Rudolf|title = Fundamental Irreversibility and the Concept of Events|journal = Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume = 132|pages = 245–252|year = 1990|issue = 1|doi = 10.1007/BF02278010|url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104201040|bibcode = 1990CMaPh.132..245H|s2cid = 120715539}} {{Cite book|last=Haag|first=Rudolf|date=2015|chapter=Faces of Quantum Physics|title=The Message of Quantum Science|series=Lecture Notes in Physics|volume=899|pages=219–234|publisher=Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg|isbn=978-3-662-46422-9|doi=10.1007/978-3-662-46422-9_9}} {{Cite journal|last=Haag|first=Rudolf|title=On quantum theory|journal=International Journal of Quantum Information|volume=17|number=4|year=2019|pages=1950037–1–9|doi=10.1142/S0219749919500370|bibcode=2019IJQI...1750037H|arxiv=1602.05426}}</ref>

Haag developed an interest in music at an early age. He began learning the [[violin]], but later preferred the [[piano]], which he played almost every day. In 1948, Haag married Käthe Fues,{{refn|group=note|Käthe Fues was one of the daughters of the German theoretical physicist [[Erwin Fues]].<ref>{{Cite book|date=2005|title=Wolfgang Pauli|volume=18|chapter=Das Jahr 1958 Letzte Zusammenarbeit mit Heisenberg. Die Spinortheorie der Elementarteilchen und die Genfer Hochenergiekonferenz|series=Sources in the History of Mathematics and Physical Sciences|publisher=Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg|language=de|isbn=978-3-540-26832-1|page=1186|doi=10.1007/3-540-26832-4_2}}</ref>}} with whom he had four children, Albert, Friedrich, Elisabeth, and Ulrich. After retirement, he moved together with his second wife Barbara Klie{{refn|group=note|Haag married Barbara Klie after Käthe's premature death.}} to [[Schliersee]], a pastoral village in the [[Bavaria]]n mountains. He died on 5 January 2016, in Fischhausen-Neuhaus, in southern Bavaria.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Buchholz|first1=Detlev|last2=Doplicher|first2=Sergio|last3=Fredenhagen|first3=Klaus|title=Rudolf Haag (1922 - 2016)|journal=News Bulletin, International Association of Mathematical Physics|pages=27–31|year=2016|url=http://www.iamp.org/bulletins/old-bulletins/Bulletin-January2016-print.pdf}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
At the beginning of his career, Haag contributed significantly to the concepts of quantum field theory, including [[Haag's theorem]], from which follows that the interaction picture of [[quantum mechanics]] does not exist in quantum field theory.{{refn|group=note|Haag's theorem states that the usual [[Fock space]] representation cannot be used to describe interacting relativistic quantum fields with canonical commutation relations. One needs inequivalent [[Hilbert space]] representations of fields.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Haag_theorem|title=Haag theorem|website=Encyclopedia of Mathematics|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref>}} A new approach to the description of scattering processes of particles became necessary. In the following years Haag developed what is known as [[Haag–Ruelle scattering theory]].<ref>See e.g. the review: {{Cite book|last1 = Buchholz|first1 = Detlev|last2 = Summers|first2 = Stephen J.|date = 2006|article = Scattering in Relativistic Quantum Field Theory: Fundamental Concepts and Tools|title = Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics|pages = 456–465|publisher = Academic Press|isbn = 978-0-12-512666-3|doi = 10.1016/B0-12-512666-2/00018-3|arxiv = math-ph/0509047|s2cid = 16258638}}</ref>

During this work, he realized that the rigid relationship between fields and particles that had been postulated up to that point, did not exist, and that the particle interpretation should be based on [[Albert Einstein]]'s principle of locality, which assigns operators to regions of spacetime. These insights found their final formulation in the [[Haag–Kastler axioms]] for local observables of quantum field theories.<ref>{{Cite book|first1=Romeo|last1=Brunetti|first2=Klaus|last2=Fredenhagen|date=2006|article=Algebraic Approach to Quantum Field Theory|title=Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics|pages=198–204|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-512666-3|doi=10.1016/B0-12-512666-2/00078-X|arxiv=math-ph/0411072|s2cid=119018200}}</ref> This framework uses elements of the theory of [[operator algebra]]s and is therefore referred to as [[Axiomatic quantum field theory|algebraic quantum field theory]] or, from the physical point of view, as [[Local quantum field theory|local quantum physics]].<ref>{{Cite book|last = Haag|first = Rudolf|date = 1996|edition = 2|title = Local quantum physics: Fields, particles, algebras|publisher = Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg|isbn =  978-3-540-61049-6|doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-61458-3}}</ref>

This concept proved fruitful for understanding the fundamental properties of any theory in four-dimensional [[Minkowski space]]. Without making assumptions about non-observable charge-changing fields, Haag, in collaboration with [[Sergio Doplicher]] and John E. Roberts, elucidated the possible structure of the [[superselection sectors]] of the observables in theories with short-range forces.{{refn|group=note|The only additional assumption to the Haag–Kastler axioms for the observables in this analysis was the postulate of the Haag duality, which was later established by Joseph J. Bisognano and [[Eyvind Wichmann|Eyvind H. Wichmann]] in the framework of quantum field theory; the discussion of infinite statistics was also dispensed with.}} Sectors can always be composed with one another, each sector satisfies either para-[[Bose–Einstein statistics|Bose]] or para-[[Fermi–Dirac statistics|Fermi]] statistics and for each sector there is a conjugate sector. These insights correspond to the additivity of charges in the particle interpretation, to the Bose–Fermi alternative for particle statistics, and to the existence of [[antiparticle]]s. In the special case of simple sectors, a global [[Gauge group (mathematics)|gauge group]] and charge-carrying fields, which can generate all sectors from the vacuum state, were reconstructed from the observables.<ref>{{Cite book|last = Fredenhagen|first = Klaus|date = 2015|chapter = An Introduction to Algebraic Quantum Field Theory|title = Advances in Algebraic Quantum Field Theory|series = Mathematical Physics Studies|pages = 1–30|publisher = Springer International Publishing|isbn = 978-3-319-21352-1|doi = 10.1007/978-3-319-21353-8_1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Doplicher|first1=Sergio|last2=Haag|first2=Rudolf|last3=Roberts|first3=John E.|title=Fields, observables and gauge transformations I|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=13|pages=1–23|year=1969|issue=1|doi=10.1007/BF01645267|url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1103841481|bibcode=1969CMaPh..13....1D|s2cid=123420887}} {{Cite journal|last1=Doplicher|first1=Sergio|last2=Haag|first2=Rudolf|last3=Roberts|first3=John E.|title=Fields, observables and gauge transformations II|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=15|pages=173–200|year=1969|issue=3|doi=10.1007/BF01645674|url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1103841943|bibcode=1969CMaPh..15..173D|s2cid=189831020|url-access=subscription}}</ref> These results were later generalized for arbitrary sectors in the [[Tannaka–Krein duality#Doplicher–Roberts theorem|Doplicher–Roberts duality theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Doplicher|first1=Sergio|last2=Roberts|first2=John E.|title=A new duality theory for compact groups|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=98|pages=157–218|year=1989|doi=10.1007/BF01388849|bibcode=1989InMat..98..157D|s2cid=120280418}} {{Cite journal|last1=Doplicher|first1=Sergio|last2=Roberts|first2=John E.|title=Why there is a field algebra with a compact gauge group describing the superselection structure in particle physics|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=131|pages=51–107|year=1990|issue=1|doi=10.1007/BF02097680|url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104200703|bibcode=1990CMaPh.131...51D|s2cid=121071316}}</ref> The application of these methods to theories in low-dimensional spaces also led to an understanding of the occurrence of [[braid group]] statistics and [[quantum group]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fredenhagen|first1=Klaus|last2=Rehren|first2=Karl-Henning|last3=Schroer|first3=Bert|title=Superselection Sectors with Braid Group Statistics and Exchange Algebras. 1. General Theory|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=125|pages=201|year=1989|issue=2|doi=10.1007/BF01217906|url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104179464|bibcode=1989CMaPh.125..201F|s2cid=122633954|url-access=subscription}} {{Cite journal|last1=Fredenhagen|first1=Klaus|last2=Rehren|first2=Karl-Henning|last3=Schroer|first3=Bert|title=Superselection sectors with braid group statistics and exchange algebras. 2. Geometric aspects and conformal covariance|journal=Reviews in Mathematical Physics|volume=4|pages=113–157|year=1992|doi=10.1142/S0129055X92000170|bibcode=1992RvMaP...4S.113F}} {{Cite journal|last1=Froehlich|first1=Juerg|last2=Gabbiani|first2=Fabrizio|title=Braid statistics in local quantum theory|journal=Reviews in Mathematical Physics|volume=2|pages=251–354|year=1991|issue=3|doi=10.1142/S0129055X90000107}}</ref>

In [[quantum statistical mechanics]], Haag, together with [[Nicolaas Marinus Hugenholtz|Nicolaas M. Hugenholtz]] and Marinus Winnink, succeeded in generalizing the [[Josiah Willard Gibbs|Gibbs]]–[[John von Neumann|von Neumann]] characterization of thermal equilibrium states using the [[Tomita–Takesaki theory#KMS states|KMS condition]] (named after [[Ryogo Kubo]], Paul C. Martin, and [[Julian Schwinger]]) in such a way that it extends to infinite systems in the [[thermodynamic limit]]. It turned out that this condition also plays a prominent role in the theory of [[von Neumann algebra]]s and resulted in the [[Tomita–Takesaki theory]]. This theory has proven to be a central element in structural analysis and recently{{refn|group=note|It is referred to the algebraic [[constructive quantum field theory|constructive quantum field theories]] born at the beginning of this century. They are different respect to the constructive theories mathematically developed in the 70s and 80s inspired by semiclassical ideas. See for example Summers' historical overview.<ref>{{cite web|last=Summers|first=Stephen|url=https://people.clas.ufl.edu/sjs/constructive-quantum-field-theory/|title=Constructive Quantum Field Theory|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Florida|access-date=January 9, 2021}}</ref>}} also in the construction of concrete quantum field theoretical models.{{refn|group=note|An overview of the construction of a large number of models using these methods can be found in Lechner's chapter.<ref>{{Cite book|last = Lechner|first = Gandalf|date = 2015|chapter = Algebraic Constructive Quantum Field Theory: Integrable Models and Deformation Techniques|title = Advances in Algebraic Quantum Field Theory|series = Mathematical Physics Studies|pages = 397–448|publisher = Springer International Publishing|isbn = 978-3-319-21352-1|doi = 10.1007/978-3-319-21353-8| bibcode=2015aaqf.book.....B }}</ref>}} Together with [[Daniel Kastler]] and Ewa Trych-Pohlmeyer, Haag also succeeded in deriving the KMS condition from the stability properties of thermal equilibrium states.<ref>{{Cite book|first=Christian D.|last=Jäkel|date=2006|article=Thermal Quantum Field Theory|title=Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics|pages=227–235|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-512666-3|doi=10.1016/B0-12-512666-2/00089-4}}</ref> Together with [[Huzihiro Araki]], Daniel Kastler, and [[Masamichi Takesaki]], he also developed a theory of [[chemical potential]] in this context.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Longo|first=Roberto|title=Notes for a quantum index theorem|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=222|pages=45–96|year=2001|issue=1|doi=10.1007/s002200100492|arxiv=math/0003082|bibcode=2001CMaPh.222...45L|s2cid=14305468}}</ref>

The framework created by Haag and Kastler for studying quantum field theories in Minkowski space can be transferred to theories in curved spacetime. By working with [[Klaus Fredenhagen]], Heide Narnhofer, and Ulrich Stein, Haag made important contributions to the understanding of the [[Unruh effect]] and [[Hawking radiation]].<ref>{{Cite book|first = Bernard S.|last = Kay|date = 2006|article = Quantum Field Theory in Curved Spacetime|title = Encyclopedia of Mathematical Physics|pages = 202–212|publisher = Academic Press|isbn = 978-0-12-512666-3|doi = 10.1016/B0-12-512666-2/00018-3|arxiv = gr-qc/0601008|s2cid = 16258638}}</ref>

Haag had a certain mistrust towards what he viewed as speculative developments in [[theoretical physics]]{{refn|group=note|He was critical of [[string theory]], blaming a misunderstanding of the concept of particle in the conventional framework of quantum field theory.<ref name=Haag2010 />}} but occasionally dealt with such questions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jaeger|first=Gregg|title=The Ontology of Haag's Local Quantum Physics|journal=Entropy|volume=26|pages=33|year=2023|issue=1|doi=10.3390/e26010033|doi-access=free |pmid=38248159 |pmc=10814221|bibcode=2023Entrp..26...33J }}</ref> The best known Acontribution is the [[Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius theorem]], which classifies the possible [[Supersymmetry|supersymmetries]] of the [[S-matrix]] that are not covered by the [[Coleman–Mandula theorem]].{{refn|group=note|The theorem of [[Sidney Coleman]] and [[Jeffrey Mandula]] excludes a nontrivial coupling of bosonic inner symmetry groups with geometric symmetries ([[Poincaré group]]). The supersymmetry, on the other hand, allows such a coupling.}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Maldacena|first=Juan Martin|author-link1=Juan Maldacena|title=The Large N limit of superconformal field theories and supergravity|journal=Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics|volume=2|pages=231–252|year=1998|issue=4|doi=10.1023/A:1026654312961|arxiv = hep-th/9711200|s2cid=12613310}} {{Cite book|last=Martin|first=Stephen P.|title=Perspectives on Supersymmetry II|chapter=A Supersymmetry Primer|journal=Advanced Series on Directions in High Energy Physics|volume=21|pages=1–153|year=2010|doi=10.1142/9789814307505_0001|arxiv = hep-ph/9709356|bibcode=2010pesu.book....1M|isbn=978-981-4307-48-2}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1970, Haag received the [[Max Planck Medal]] for outstanding achievements in theoretical physics<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/max-planck-medaille/preistraeger|title=Max Planck Medal Prize winners|website=German Physical Society|language=de|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref> and in 1997 the [[Henri Poincaré Prize]]<ref>
{{cite web |url=http://www.iamp.org/page.php?page=page_prize_poincare|title=Henri Poincaré Prize winners|website=International Association of Mathematical Physics|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref> for his fundamental contributions to quantum field theory as one of the founders of the modern formulation.<ref name=HP_citation /> Since 1980, Haag was a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]<ref>
{{cite web |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/rudolf-haag/|title=German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina member page of Rudolf Haag|website=German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref> and since 1981 of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Göttingen Academy of Sciences]].<ref>
{{cite web|url=https://adw-goe.de/en/members/personendetails/person/Rudolf-Haag/|language=de|title=Göttingen Academy of Sciences member page of Rudolf Haag|website=Göttingen Academy of Sciences|access-date=3 March 2021}} {{Cite book|date = 2011|title = Jahrbuch der Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen 2010|editor = Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen|publisher = De Gruyter|isbn = 978-3110236767|language=de|doi = 10.26015/adwdocs-386|author1 = (:Unkn) Unknown}}</ref> Since 1979, he was a corresponding member of the [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Bavarian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://badw.de/en/data/footer-navigation/personentreffer.html?tx_badwdb_badwperson%5Bper_id%5D=1113&tx_badwdb_badwperson%5BpartialType%5D=BADWPersonDetailsPartial&tx_badwdb_badwperson%5Baction%5D=show&tx_badwdb_badwperson%5Bcontroller%5D=BADWPerson|title=Bavarian Academy of Sciences member page of Rudolf Haag|website=Bavarian Academy of Sciences|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref> and since 1987 of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/en/members-commissions/members-of-the-oeaw/all-members-at-a-glance/m/haag-rudolf|title=Austrian Academy of Sciences member page of Rudolf Haag|website=Austrian Academy of Sciences|access-date=9 January 2021|archive-date=12 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112215723/https://www.oeaw.ac.at/en/members-commissions/members-of-the-oeaw/all-members-at-a-glance/m/haag-rudolf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
